title: Round Complexity of Iterated Prefix-Counting Programs—Tight Bounds for Multiplication and Montgomery Reduction
content: We investigate the round complexity of deterministic sequence programs with a fixed finite state per position, pointwise operations, prefix counts, and fixed-radius backward Boolean lookups. We establish a cut-capacity inequality: the number of distinct rows of the communication matrix for any admissible right-side output is at most the product of the per-round cut-message alphabets. We then determine exact row counts for binary multiplication and for two precisely specified versions of Montgomery reduction. For bounded-support counting, these lower bounds imply linear round complexity. Explicit, uniform constructions attain linear upper bounds using a constant-size step with support-one counters for multiplication and lazy Montgomery reduction, and a fixed four-phase public schedule for canonical reduction. We give exact encoding contracts, distinguish one-way cut information from ordinary circuit depth, and describe computational verification of finite instances. The theorem concerns a defined symbolic model and does not assert a lower bound for arbitrary softmax transformers.
